analysis:
Examined both test files, patches, surrounding BASE/HEAD source and file metadata against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift HEAD 68–109 now expects declared model/artifact families to receive public-qualified status without passing records; mismatched explicit artifacts, undeclared models and undeclared families remain negative cases. HEAD 111–125 tests the speculative assistant's public-status exclusion, but only through publicTrafficLine. HEAD 132–138 and ClusterPairServingDecisionsTests.swift patch HEAD 157–159 explicitly disable declarations to retain record-only assertions. Existing owner-serving, divergence, rank/mode refusal and time-budget tests are otherwise unchanged.
No concrete security regression is established by these test-only units: they neither implement routing nor demonstrate an authorization bypass, plaintext exposure, cache-isolation change, billing change or privileged execution. The changed expectations are relevant to T-007/T-027 computation integrity and TB-002/TB-011's distinction between provider claims and coordinator permission, not proof that model parity qualification equals App Attest serving authorization. T-041 cache bindings and crypto are not changed here.
Integration must examine ClusterPublicModels and ClusterPairServingGrants implementations and their changed offer/admission callers: verify declarations do not bypass authoritative placement qualification or connection authorization; verify actual artifact binding when artifactSHA256 is omitted (HEAD 82); and verify assistant exclusion prevents coordinator offers/admission rather than merely changing the display string (HEAD 118–123). Those controls are outside this source scope, not observed missing controls. Remaining uncertainty is material because the tests newly describe public qualification without records.
